chunks: Al-Saffār narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Ziyād ibn Abī al-Ḥallāl, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Yaʿfūr, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: What do you say regarding the blood of fleas? He said: “There is no harm in it.” He said: I said: It becomes abundant and excessive. He said: “Even if it is abundant.” He said: I said: Then a man may have spots of blood on his garment and not know of it; then he comes to know of it but forgets to wash it and so he performs salat (prayer), then remembers after he has prayed—must he repeat his salat (prayer)? He said: “He should wash it and not repeat his salat (prayer), unless it is collected to the measure of a dirham; then he should wash it and repeat the salat (prayer).”

key_terms.دَمِ الْبَرَاغِيثِ: the blood of fleas, discussed here as not objectionable for salat (prayer)
key_terms.لَيْسَ بِهِ بَأْسٌ: there is no harm or problem in it
key_terms.مِقْدَارَ الدِّرْهَمِ: the measure of a dirham, used as a legal threshold here
key_terms.نُقَطُ الدَّمِ: spots or small marks of blood on a garment

ai.seo_question: Does blood on clothing invalidate salat (prayer), and what is the ruling on flea blood?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on blood found on clothing, especially the blood of fleas, stating that there is no problem with it even when it is abundant. It also explains that if a person prayed while forgetting about blood on his garment, he does not repeat the salat (prayer) unless the blood had gathered to the amount of a dirham.
